% The class writes the abstract to a file verbatim, so the text stands here
% and cannot be read with \input.  Journal limit: 250 words.
\begin{abstract}
Agents built on large language models now automate data-science work. Such
an agent holds knowledge about how to build a model in four places: the language model, the harness around it,
an AutoML library and an instruction file written by experts. A general
scheme separates these places, and three hypotheses state which of them
decides accuracy and reliability.
One open-weight 31B model runs under three harnesses: FEDOT.LLM (a
fixed-stage workflow over an AutoML library), AutoDS-Tools (a six-agent
system) and Terminus-2 (a minimal shell agent). Accuracy is scaled per task from 0 (weakest) to 1 (strongest) of the
eighteen tuned methods published with TabReD. H1, the harness alone does not decide accuracy:
without the instruction file the three harnesses score $\nTerminus$ to
$\nFedot$, no pairwise difference is significant, and they differ in run
time and reliability. H2, accuracy follows the part that holds and applies
the knowledge of search and tuning: agents writing their own code fit one untuned
gradient-boosting model. An instruction that hands the modelling to an
AutoML library raises AutoDS-Tools from $\nAutoDSOff$ to $\nAutoDS$, the
level of tuned LightGBM and below the strongest published method
($\nBest$). H3, explicit knowledge and the language model change reliability in a
direction set by the harness: moved to Terminus-2, the same instruction file
ends \ktBothLost{} of 24 trials without a submission. A larger model removes
such trials in one harness and adds them in the other. Instructions and
language models must therefore be evaluated with their harness.
\end{abstract}

% The class prints the highlights on a page of their own before the title
% page.  At submission they also go as a separate editable file.
\begin{highlights}
\item Agentic AutoML holds knowledge in the model, harness, AutoML library and instructions
\item Without instructions, three harnesses reach similar accuracy at different run times
\item Accuracy rises when an AutoML library applies the knowledge of search and tuning
\item Explicit knowledge written for one harness costs submissions in another
\item No configuration reaches the strongest tuned method published with the benchmark
\end{highlights}

\begin{keywords}
automated machine learning \sep LLM agents \sep agent harness \sep
agent skills \sep explicit knowledge \sep parametric knowledge \sep tabular learning
\end{keywords}
